body:
Batch 8/GPU left substantial throughput available on the eight B300s. This follow-up implements the user-authorized precision/compiler arm, repairs exact profile admission, and applies a measured R4 batch continuation: **96/GPU for 630M and 64/GPU for 1.54B**, four fresh 30-epoch fits at W2. [Live PR32 progress](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/32#issuecomment-6377032958) separates successful updates from evaluated fits.

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Follow-up to #32; teacher-size lineage; SemyonEpanov. Scientific source is pinned to `f1beeb4c210a9da01735e03b1ff6e27be878b873`, separately from later operator/documentation commits. Four full fits run under `pr32-teachers-20261024-r4-batch`; zero evaluated endpoints are claimed at this handoff.

2. **Why it should work.** Larger batches amortize CPU/loading, launch, DDP and Muon overhead across more rows. BF16 model compute, cuBLAS BF16x9 FP32 emulation, exact-window efficient attention, block compilation and activation recomputation off improve measured throughput. FP32 master parameters/gradients/loss/optimizer state remain; process-global BF16x9 can affect Muon GEMMs and is not an IEEE-identical FP32 reproduction.

3. **Compute advantage.** Warm W2 rates rose from 35.6k to 116.9k rows/s for 630M and 25.4k to 61.0k for 1.54B, approximately 3.29x/2.41x. Small B128 also completed 12 updates, but was slower than96 and used 260.8 GiB. The selected R4 four-cell profiles reserve 196.0/231.4 GiB per GPU. Compute-only fitting projects about 33.6 h; measured nonwindow loading/logging overhead raises the projection to 34.9 h. Cold startup, checkpoints, export/evaluation and collection remain additional; completed epochs will recalibrate the estimate.

4. **Frozen recipe and amendment.** Original seeds 101001/101002 by F0/F2, scratch initialization, raw causal 112 inputs, exact 1024-row local window, detached 512-row TBPTT, eight time chunks/update, labels-only objective, fitting-only normalization and fixed-final 30 epochs remain. R4 global batches are 192/128. LR stays 3e-4; Muon/AdamW, clipping, weight decay and 5% warmup/cosine policy remain, with the update horizon recalculated. The original strict-FP32 recipe and earlier batches are preserved as history.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** Exactly four new full teacher fits, two per width, no trained-control reuse and no student fits. Small fits require 9,450 updates each; large fits 14,100: 47,100 total. R2 was deliberately superseded with 1,842/448,500 updates, zero completed fits, retained logs and available safe checkpoints. R3 comprised profiles only. The user chose the full experiment rather than the historical 4-hour campaign. Seven-day per-job failsafes bound stalls; no retry queue.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Official held-out scoring and masks remain unchanged on exposed F0/F2. Width and batch now co-vary: endpoints compare complete teacher recipes, not an isolated architecture-size effect. Two coupled fold/seed cells do not establish broad statistical significance. Throughput and finite-loss checks establish neither quality equivalence nor student-transfer/public-score gain.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Canonical component-qualified split hashes are fixed; both widths share the same split within each fold. Normalizers use fitting members only, no trained parent initializes these teachers, and exact causal prefix checks remain. No held-out score selected a batch. Previously inspected folds remain exposed.

8. **Decision-changing result.** All ten batch candidates completed 12 real-data updates without OOM or optimizer-state errors. The receiving validator independently recomputes profile identities, row rates, VRAM eligibility and the selection rule from raw files. The user explicitly questioned the conservative 15% reserve; R4 uses 10%, admitting large B64 with about 13.5% observed headroom. Full endpoint validation and eventual student benefit determine model promotion. One earlier synthetic Muon compiled/eager update differed by relative-L2 .0877; this remains an explicit numerical-arm difference.

9. **Execution.** A finite self-hash-bound controller validates source/config/data/split/runtime/profile identities, exact batch authority, eight unique GPU UUIDs and 32 CPU IDs. A native cron PAM session owns fitting independently of SSH. Each owned group executes fit -> held-out export -> official score, saves epoch-safe state and releases its GPUs. No foreign process cleanup, automatic scientific retries or conditional 40-fit expansion.

10. **Evidence and reporting.** The [execution packet](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/pr32-blackwell-throughput-20261024/research/experiment_drafts/b300-transformer-distillation-runtime/execution_20261024/README.md) indexes R4's plan, resource estimate, CPU diagnostic, raw profiles, operators and hashed archive. On one training-matched CPU thread, B64/96/128 assembly took 1.43/2.05/2.85s and H2D .05/.08/.10s; each batch supplies five updates. Hourly and evaluated-completion/terminal updates publish as SemyonEpanov in the original PR32 comment. Weights remain on approved node storage.

11. **Validation and merge.** The unchanged scientific source passed 77 tests; the batch controller passes seven focused stdlib tests. Real receiving-host profiles bind all four actual production cells. The original optimizer tuple/list JSON admission defect is fixed at the metadata producer without weakening exact admission or changing optimizer values; its failed zero-update start is preserved. Merge after #32. This draft hands off running experiments and reproducible engineering evidence, not a completed quality result.
